title: Role lifecycle, SSO group mapping, and admin controls — Console RBAC v2 UX
creator: Sofia Gomez
description: Problem: RBAC v1 in Console is limited: roles are monolithic, SSO group mapping is ad-hoc, and admins lack an opinionated workflow for creating, auditing, and retiring roles. Goal: design a role lifecycle UX that supports role creation, editing, versioned changes, SSO/group mapping, member assignment, and clear admin controls (least-privilege guidance, staging/canary of role changes). This ticket covers the end-to-end UI flows and the migration affordances to help existing customers move from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 without breaking access or losing auditability.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Role create/edit flow supports: name, description, scoped permissions (resource + action), expiration policy, and optional justification field.
2) SSO mapping UI: map one or more SSO groups to a role, visualize live group membership, and offer a preview of members before commit.
3) Member assignment supports bulk add/remove, conflict warnings, and shows the origin of assignment (direct vs SSO).
4) Admin controls panel surfaces: role usage metrics, last-used timestamps for permissions, and a one-click 'least-privilege recommendation' that suggests revoked permissions.
5) Role changes are staged and can be rolled out via canary, scheduled, or immediate modes; the UI shows rollouts and fallbacks.
6) Audit trail: every change to roles, mappings, and assignments appears in console audit logs with who/what/when and links to the change event in Console.
7) Migration helper: import existing roles and map them to new scoped permissions with a diff preview and rollback option.
8) Usability: prototype usability test (n=6) should reach 90% task completion for creating a scoped role and mapping an SSO group.
design_notes: We propose a three-pane editor: left = role metadata and lifecycle controls, center = permission matrix with resource scoping and quick filters, right = member preview with SSO group integration.

Permission units should be composable: allow toggling between 'coarse' (route/model) and 'fine' (route+method/field) granularity. Design must avoid overwhelming users; default to coarse with an 'advanced' toggle.
SSO mapping flow must include a read-only preview of group members (pulled from SAML/SCIM sync) and a simulation mode that shows effective permissions per-sample-user.
Add microcopy explaining security impacts: e.g., what 'Allow read on model X' means in practice and examples for common roles (Viewer, Deployer, Billing Admin).
Role lifecycle states: Draft -> Staged -> Active -> Deprecated. UI should show state and allow scheduled promotion and phased rollout percentages for Active.
Include a 'role health' card: last usage, number of members, number of policies referencing role, and risk score (based on permission breadth and membership size).
decisions: Use staged rollouts for role changes instead of immediate global changes — reduces blast radius and allows rollback.
Show both direct members and SSO-derived members in the same member list, with icons denoting source. This reduces confusion about who has access.
Default permission view will be coarse-grained; advanced users can expand to field/method-level permissions.
